title: Capitalism
findings: Investment, ownership, and purchasing power follow the workshop example; unequal financing is a substantive constraint, not a verification aside.

title: Socialism
findings: Worker cooperatives, markets, and planning lead into the distinction between legal ownership and actual authority without narrating sources.

title: Economic planning
findings: The ambulance example introduces planning; local information and strategic reporting explain its difficulties in the same narrative.

title: Democracy
findings: Direct decisions, representation, eligibility, and accountability are introduced before their limitations; no hidden historical dispute is invoked.

title: Meritocracy
findings: The selection example establishes unequal preparation and the limits of merit claims before discussing them.

title: Technocracy
findings: Flood protection introduces expertise and value judgments; peer review and public authority are distinguished in context.

title: Monarchy
findings: Explained the British division of authority directly rather than narrating an example and appending a generic limitation.

title: Dynasties
findings: Family succession follows the transport-company example; the GFT citation supports transmission of knowledge without narrating the book.

title: Bureaucracy
findings: The clerk example connects rules, discretion, appeals, and continuing records without unrelated methodological caveats.

title: Government
findings: The water-system example follows decisions through implementation and explains capture as a concrete risk.

title: Law
findings: The path dispute introduces adjudication and access; rule-of-law constraints are explained rather than presented as source notes.

title: Diplomacy
findings: The diplomatic discussion distinguishes exploratory contact from authority to commit; the final uncertainty follows that distinction.

title: Political theory
findings: The topic is political theory itself, so explaining legitimacy theories is substantive rather than a narrated research detour.

title: Ideology
findings: The different meanings of ideology are needed to understand the topic; the factory example and habits of attention remain connected.

title: Strategy
findings: The street-safety example explains diagnosis, coordinated action, and revision without source narration.

title: Education
findings: Learning, credentials, and educational opportunity follow a shared question about transmitting capability.

title: Cities
findings: Density, costs, and access are connected through the repair-shop and urban-space examples.

title: Healthcare
findings: The care pathway explains coordination gaps; the distinction between coverage and effective care is directly relevant.

title: Psychotherapy
findings: Removed a disclaimer about what this overview does; retained professional boundaries and method-specific uncertainty in the explanation.

title: Marriage
findings: Replaced an unsolicited warning about judging relationship worth with a conclusion following the rights-and-power discussion.

title: Adoption
findings: Child adoption is explained before historical adult succession is distinguished; the differing purposes are made explicit.

title: Ritual
findings: The fire-walking study is introduced as a concrete example of different responses among participants, not as an unexplained literature dispute.

title: Sacrifice
findings: Connected the theory to a mechanism and its actual dependency instead of a detached non-proof caveat.
Removed an unsolicited disclaimer already addressed by the preceding distinction between voluntary contribution and coerced compliance.

title: Marketing
findings: The theater offer connects audience, feedback, and measurement to the marketing mechanism.

title: Social norms
findings: The lateness example establishes expectations before discussing mismatches between formal rules and practice.

title: Sociocracy
findings: Circles, consent, and double linking are explained as components with direct source links and no research diary.

title: Polycentric governance
findings: The river example makes cross-boundary dependencies and overlapping authority understandable before discussing their costs.

title: Open-source ecosystems
findings: Licensing, maintenance, governance, and forking form a connected account of the work around an open project.

title: Extitutional theory
findings: Kept the framework’s explanatory scope while replacing generic recipe language with observable relational questions.

title: Assembly democracy
findings: Attendance and authority are distinguished from the beginning; referendum comparison is introduced explicitly.

title: Direct democracy
findings: The referendum and assembly examples explain direct decision-making before agenda control and participation demands.

title: Representative democracy
findings: Delegation of political work leads directly to elections, public records, and accountability between votes.

title: Participation-based alignment
findings: Returned the ending to the festival example instead of closing with a generic audit instruction.

title: Mutual recognition
findings: Replaced a warning against scoring that had not been proposed with the actual transition from recognition to authority.

title: Informal authority
findings: Informal authority is established through the meeting example; the venue contact explains how dependency develops.

title: Cliques and informal exclusion
findings: Friendship and control over collective decisions are distinguished through the private-conversation example.

title: Economic embeddedness
findings: Supplier trust explains both access and exclusion; the final questions follow those concrete relationships.

title: Weak-tie bridges
findings: The acquaintance example explains network reach while the crisis comparison distinguishes it from close support.

title: Learning through participation
findings: Event volunteering connects practical learning to access, feedback, and growing responsibility.

title: Core and peripheral participation
findings: The reading-group example explains varying participation and the difficulty of moving in or out of central roles.

title: Stigmergic coordination
findings: The repair list introduces shared traces; conventions and neglected work explain the mechanism’s limits.

title: Growth outrunning onboarding
findings: Removed source narration and an unintroduced claim that all growth destroys communities; connected the citation to the onboarding constraint.

title: Tacit knowledge dependence
findings: The caretaker example makes tacit judgment concrete and connects it to procedures and handovers.

title: Institutional imitation
findings: The copied advisory board and review process introduce the difference between visible form and functioning capability.

title: Founder dependence
findings: Founder judgment is connected to relationships, succession, tacit knowledge, and delegated authority without a book-summary frame.

title: Homophily
findings: Recruiting friends explains homophily; distinguishing preference from opportunity is essential to the mechanism.

title: Reciprocity
findings: Explained the indirect-reciprocity mechanism directly instead of announcing a research topic.

title: Trust formation and repair
findings: Attached the evidence to the specific difference in repair rather than narrating the study.

title: Free riding
findings: Connected the experiment to the established issue of unequal capacity to contribute, replacing a generic disclaimer.

title: Social loafing
findings: The committee example distinguishes motivational withdrawal from unclear responsibility and blocked dependencies.

title: Volunteer burnout
findings: Retained attribution to former volunteers while removing an irrelevant warning about diagnosing every tired volunteer.

title: Status hierarchies
findings: Stated the relative-status mechanism with a supporting link rather than describing what research explains.

title: Preference falsification
findings: The public agreement example introduces hidden preferences; the limits distinguish silence from actual concealment.

title: Pluralistic ignorance
findings: The long-meeting example introduces misperception; the drinking study is a bounded example of the same distinction.

title: Group polarization
findings: The proposal discussion establishes polarization and makes diversity of information a concrete concern.

title: Groupthink
findings: Contested groupthink explanations are directly relevant because the page explains how to avoid inferring decision processes from bad outcomes alone.

title: Goal displacement
findings: The application form makes goal displacement concrete; rule revision follows the same problem.

title: Metric gaming
findings: Case-closing metrics explain both improvement and avoidance; the distinction between score and purpose remains grounded.

title: Capture
findings: Replaced a rebuttal to the unintroduced claim that every regulator is captured with the actual distinction between contact and distorted decisions.

title: Principal-agent problems
findings: The contractor example establishes asymmetric information and conflicting interests before considering controls.

title: Path dependence
findings: The record-system example explains switching costs; distinguishing persistence from lock-in prevents misidentifying the mechanism.

title: Norm drift
findings: Kept the term descriptive while removing a claim about what theory had not been established.
Made the experimental scope explicit and connected it back to the response-time example instead of adding a generic transfer-limit sentence.

title: Network brokerage
findings: Replaced an abstract causality disclaimer with the missing work between access to ideas and useful cooperation.

title: Boundary maintenance
findings: The newcomer example introduces boundaries; confidentiality and competence requirements are concrete contrasts to unspoken exclusion.
